headline: Both segments post double-digit growth as margins expand
summary_short: HEICO's Q2 FY2026 net sales rose 25% y/y (+17% q/q) to a record $1,375.7M, with net income up 49% y/y to $233.8M ($1.66 diluted EPS) as both the Flight Support and Electronic Technologies segments posted double-digit organic growth.
summary_long: Net sales rose 25% y/y and 17% q/q to a record $1,375.7M, as FSG grew 21% (19% organic) and ETG grew 34% (17% organic) on demand for aftermarket parts, repair/overhaul, and defense/aerospace electronics. Gross margin expanded to 41.4% from 39.9% y/y on favorable mix in both segments; SG&A fell to 15.9% of sales on scale efficiencies. Operating income rose 41% y/y to $350.4M (25.5% margin, up from 22.6%). Net income attributable to HEICO rose 49% y/y to $233.8M, or $1.66 diluted EPS. Cash was $210.3M after $821.3M of acquisition spending this year, funded largely by revolver draws; total debt-to-equity was 53.3%. Management now guides FY2026 capex to $85-95M.

drivers.explanation: FSG net sales +21% ($162.4M) on 19% organic growth (aftermarket parts +$102.4M, specialty products +$22.7M, repair/overhaul +$19.7M) plus acquisitions; ETG net sales +34% ($117.4M) on 17% organic growth (other electronics, defense, aerospace, space products) plus acquisitions.

Consolidated gross margin rose to 41.4% from 39.9%, principally a 2.7ppt improvement in ETG's margin (favorable aerospace product mix, higher sales) and a 0.8ppt improvement in FSG's margin (favorable aftermarket parts mix).
FSG operating income +31% on net sales growth, SG&A efficiencies, and improved gross margin; ETG operating income +56% on net sales growth, improved gross margin, and SG&A efficiencies.
Y/y increase principally reflects the higher consolidated operating income described above; effective tax rate was roughly flat (21.2% vs 21.0%).

Record quarter for both segments; management's outlook expects continued net sales growth at FSG and ETG supported by underlying demand and recent acquisitions, with capital allocation balanced between organic growth and further M&A.
